pyth.front: What does HTTP stand for, and what is it used for?
pyth.back: Hypertext Transfer Protocol — fetching the documents you see in a browser

pyth.front: What kind of protocol is HTTP?
pyth.back: Request-response: a client connects and the server accepts; the client sends a request, and the server sends back a response
A uniform resource locator: where a piece of information you want is

pyth.text: A URL gives first the {{c1::scheme}}, which says which protocol is used; then the {{c2::host}}, plus optionally a {{c3::port}}; and after the slash, the {{c4::document or resource}} you want

pyth.front: What are HTTP verbs, and which is the simplest?
pyth.back: Words that describe what you want done; the simplest is GET

pyth.text: The first line of an HTTP request: the {{c1::verb}}, a space, {{c2::the rest of the URL after the scheme, host and port}}, a space, and {{c3::the protocol version}}

pyth.front: What are HTTP headers, and how is each one written?
pyth.back: Extra information after the first line — think of them as parameters. Each is a word, a colon, a space, then the information.

pyth.front: Which header is required in an HTTP request, and how does a request show it has ended?
pyth.back: Host; and a blank line ends the request

pyth.front: How does an HTTP response begin?
pyth.back: With the protocol, then the status code — such as the famous 404 — and then some headers

pyth.text: HTTP status codes: the 200s, {{c1::everything is fine}}; the 300s, {{c2::something is off — usually a redirect}}; the 400s, {{c3::the client did something wrong}}; the 500s, {{c4::the server did something wrong}}
pyth.extra: From the server's side the 500s are “I did something wrong”, and the 400s “you did”.

pyth.front: Which HTTP version is in plain human-readable text, and which is the latest?
pyth.back: HTTP/1.1 is plain text; HTTP/3 is the latest

pyth.front: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
pyth.back: It's secure HTTP, which most web servers use: the same protocol, but the requests and responses are encrypted, and the server proves to the client that it is who it says it is

pyth.front: Under HTTPS, how does a server prove who it is?
pyth.back: A trusted authority vouches for it. Authorities vouch for each other, in a chain that ends at a root certificate built into the OS, which is trusted implicitly.

pyth.front: Which part of Python's library makes HTTP requests, and how do you make one?
pyth.back: urllib.request. Create a Request, initialised with a URL, and pass it to urlopen, which gives back a response object.

pyth.front: On a response object, what do .status, .headers and .close() do?
pyth.back: .status gives the status code; .headers gives the headers and acts like a dictionary; .close() closes the response

pyth.front:
What does this print?
for x in response.headers:
    print(f'{x}: {response.headers[x]}')
pyth.back: Each header of the response, one per line, as Name: value

pyth.front: What does response.read() return, and how do you turn it into a str?
pyth.back: All the response's content, as bytes — Python may display it like a string, but it's still bytes. Call .decode(), passing the encoding as a keyword argument: in this class, probably utf-8.

pyth.front: How do you turn a str into bytes?
pyth.back: Call .encode() on it, with the encoding

pyth.front: How can Python serve the current directory over HTTP on localhost?
Why isn't the page you get from a YouTube search a file in a directory?
pyth.back: Web pages aren't just files in a directory any more: the URL carries your query, and the page is built for it

pyth.text: After the {{c1::?}} in a URL come the query parameters, separated by {{c2::&}}; each has a name and a value, separated by {{c3::=}}

pyth.back: The URL's escape sequences: a % followed by a character's code, as in %20 for a space

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid” (Arbaʿīn 9)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Abū Hurayrah RA

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What was Abū Hurayrah's full name, and what does “Abū Hurayrah” mean?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr. It means “father of the kitten”, a nickname the Prophet ﷺ gave him.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: When did Abū Hurayrah RA accept Islam, and which group of Companions was he among?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: In 7 AH, the year of Khaybar. He was one of <bdi>أَهْل الصُّفَّة</bdi> (ahl al-ṣuffah), the poor Companions who lived at the Prophet's ﷺ mosque.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How many aḥādīth did Abū Hurayrah RA narrate?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: 5,374 — the most of anyone

arbaeen_ahadith.text: Why Arbaʿīn 9 matters: al-Nawawī counts it among {{c1::the important principles of the dīn}}; it is from {{c2::<bdi>جَوَامِع الكَلِم</bdi>}}; and it stresses {{c3::holding to the teachings of the Sunnah}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What was the background to the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: The Prophet ﷺ said that Ḥajj is obligatory. Someone asked whether it was every year, and he stayed silent three times; then he said that had he said yes, it would have become obligatory, and too hard. So: don't ask about what he has left unspecified.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid” (Arbaʿīn 9), what does the Prophet ﷺ say to do with what he commanded?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: “What I have commanded you, do of it as much as you are able”
arbaeen_ahadith.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 9 — the text in translation

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid”, what does “avoid what I have forbidden” cover?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Both the disliked and the outright ḥarām, from the Qurʾān and the Sunnah. Avoiding them is important, and rewarded.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid”, what does “do as much of it as you can” cover, and why only as much as we can?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Both the encouraged and the obligatory, from the Qurʾān and the Sunnah. We are weak by nature and not perfect, but we're required to give our best effort.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What two causes of earlier nations' downfall does the ḥadīth “what I have forbidden you, avoid” name?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Excessive questioning — unnecessary, or meant to avoid an obligation, like the Banū Isrāʾīl and the cow — and disagreeing with their prophets

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How do scholars rank avoiding prohibitions against following commands?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: As equally important, or even more important

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What is the best way to draw closer to Allah, according to the notes on Arbaʿīn 9?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Obeying His commands, above all the obligations: the best way to grow in His love and attain His mercy. The first focus is the obligations, and the most important of them is the prayer.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does <bdi>لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا</bdi> (2:286) refer to, according to the notes on Arbaʿīn 9?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Religious obligations, not trials — it is probably the most misquoted verse of the Qurʾān

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why is “we're not required to be perfect” not an excuse to skip acts we don't like?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Because we all have the capacity to obey Allah's commands. Allah wants ease for us, not hardship (2:185), and the religion is ease — but that ease is the capacity to obey.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does Arbaʿīn 9 teach about asking questions?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Some questions are useless or have an ulterior purpose; good questions are encouraged

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Who narrates the ḥadīth “Allah is good and accepts only what is good” (Arbaʿīn 10)?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Abū Hurayrah RA

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Why is the ḥadīth “Allah is good and accepts only what is good” one of the foundations of Islam?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It describes deeds and their intention, and it stresses lawful sustenance

arbaeen_ahadith.meaning: good, pure, wholesome and healthy; as Allah's attribute, pure and perfect, free of any shortcoming

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Which deeds does Allah accept, according to the ḥadīth “Allah is good and accepts only what is good”?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Only the good and pure: a deed must be sincere, and done according to the Sharīʿah. Ostentation and arrogance are impurities.

arbaeen_ahadith.meaning: acceptance of a deed as correct: the legal obligation is fulfilled, as in praying properly
acceptance of a deed with reward: earning Allah's pleasure, so that two correct prayers can differ greatly in reward

arbaeen_ahadith.front: The prayer of someone who drinks wine is “not accepted for forty days”. Which acceptance does it lack?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Qabūl al-ithābah: the prayer is correct (iṣābah) but earns no reward

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What does Ibn Rajab say is ṭayyib in the believer?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: His whole being: his heart, through the faith in it; his tongue, through remembrance; and his body, through righteous deeds, the fruits of faith

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In the ḥadīth “Allah is good and accepts only what is good” (Arbaʿīn 10), what does the Prophet ﷺ say Allah commanded the believers, and which verses does he recite?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: What He commanded the messengers: “O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds” (23:51) and “O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you” (2:172)
arbaeen_ahadith.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 10 — the text in translation

arbaeen_ahadith.front: In those two verses, what are the ṭayyibāt?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: What Allah has allowed us to eat and consume

arbaeen_ahadith.front: Whose duʿāʾ, in the ḥadīth “Allah is good and accepts only what is good”, will not be answered, despite everything that should help it?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: A man who travels far, dishevelled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky — “O Lord, O Lord!” — while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful and he has been nourished by the unlawful
arbaeen_ahadith.source: Arbaʿīn Ḥadīth 10 — the text in translation

arbaeen_ahadith.text: What helps a duʿāʾ be accepted: {{c1::after the five daily prayers}}, {{c2::the last third of the night}}, {{c3::between the adhān and the iqāmah}}, {{c4::travelling}}, {{c5::sickness}}, {{c6::hardship}} and {{c7::being oppressed}}

arbaeen_ahadith.front: What prevents a duʿāʾ from being answered, according to the notes on Arbaʿīn 10?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Consuming, wearing or being sustained by the impermissible. If we don't answer Allah's call, how will He answer ours?

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does “halal and ṭayyib” compare with halal alone, and what is the ruling on seeking lawful income?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It's a higher standard: lawful, and also pure, wholesome and healthy. Seeking a lawful income is farḍ.

arbaeen_ahadith.front: How does unlawful food affect us, according to the notes on Arbaʿīn 10?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: Spiritually: as some foods harm the body, unlawful food harms the soul

arbaeen_ahadith.front: If a duʿāʾ seems unanswered, what might be happening instead?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: It may be bad for us; Allah may give it later; He may reward, bless and raise us instead; He may give it in the hereafter; or it may expiate our sins

arbaeen_ahadith.front: When will a duʿāʾ be answered, according to the notes on Arbaʿīn 10?
arbaeen_ahadith.back: When it asks for something lawful, with full faith in Allah, and avoids the things that block it

quduri.front: What does the Qurʾān say about the prayer times, and who specified them?
quduri.back: The prayer is prescribed for the believers at fixed times (4:103). Jibrīl specified them: he led the Prophet ﷺ in prayer on two days, once at the start of each time and once at its end, and said the time is what lies between.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: When does the Fajr time begin and end?
quduri.back: It begins at true dawn (<bdi>الفَجْر الصَّادِق</bdi>, also called the second dawn) and ends at sunrise, just as the disk breaks the horizon. One shouldn't pray while the sun is rising.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: How do false dawn and true dawn differ?
quduri.back: False dawn (<bdi>الفَجْر الكَاذِب</bdi>, the first) is a vertical white light that appears and then disappears. True dawn comes 15–20 minutes later, as a horizontal light.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: When does the Ẓuhr time begin?
quduri.back: At zawāl, when the sun passes its zenith
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: When does Ẓuhr end and ʿAṣr begin, according to Abū Ḥanīfah, and according to the majority?
quduri.back: Abū Ḥanīfah: when an object's shadow is twice its length. The majority, the Ṣāḥibān among them: when it equals its length. Neither counts the shadow at zawāl.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: Given the disagreement over the end of Ẓuhr, what do the Ḥanafī scholars recommend?
quduri.back: Out of caution, to pray Ẓuhr within the majority's time and ʿAṣr after Abū Ḥanīfah's — a recommendation, not binding
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: When does the ʿAṣr time end?
quduri.back: At sunset, just before the whole disk disappears below the horizon
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: When does the Maghrib time end, and how do Abū Ḥanīfah and the majority differ?
quduri.back: When the twilight disappears: the white twilight, for Abū Ḥanīfah; the red, for the majority and the Ṣāḥibān. It goes by what people see where they are, so a valley and a mountain differ.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: What are the times of ʿIshāʾ and of Witr?
quduri.back: ʿIshāʾ runs from the end of Maghrib until just before Fajr. Witr ends at the same time, but begins only once one has prayed ʿIshāʾ.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: the prayer times — class notes 2026-11-03

quduri.front: What is the recommended time for Fajr in the Ḥanafī school, and how did Imam Muḥammad reconcile the views?
quduri.back: Delayed until al-isfār, when there's a little light, not total darkness. The Shāfiʿīs and Mālikīs prefer the opposite, and both have narrations. Imam Muḥammad: begin in the dark and pray long enough that it grows light.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: When is Ẓuhr best prayed, in summer and in winter?
quduri.back: In summer, after waiting for it to cool a little; in winter, early
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Until when is it recommended to delay ʿAṣr?
quduri.back: For as long as the sun hasn't changed — in colour, or in becoming easy to look at
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is recommended for Maghrib, and what follows from it?
quduri.back: To hasten it — which is why the Ḥanafīs say there's no sunnah prayer between its adhān and iqāmah
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Until when is it recommended to delay ʿIshāʾ?
quduri.back: Until just before a third of the night has passed — the night being Maghrib to Fajr, in thirds. The Prophet ﷺ said that if it weren't a burden, he would have made this time obligatory.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: When is Witr best prayed?
quduri.back: At the end of the night, for someone who prays at night; before sleeping, for someone not in the habit or unsure of waking. It should be the last prayer of the day.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Someone prays Witr, sleeps, and then wakes in the night. What does he do?
quduri.back: Pray tahajjud, without praying Witr again
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.meaning: the call to prayer — linguistically the announcement, technically a specific announcement at specific times
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is the ruling on the adhān, and for which prayers?
quduri.back: Sunnah muʾakkadah, for the five daily prayers and Jumuʿah, and no others. It's recommended even for someone praying alone, out loud.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.meaning: saying the two shahādahs quietly and then loudly in the adhān — not in the Ḥanafī adhān, nor in Bilāl's, but a sunnah for the Shāfiʿīs
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What does the adhān of Fajr add, and where?
quduri.back: After <bdi>حَيَّ عَلَى الفَلَاحِ</bdi>: <bdi>الصَّلَاةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّوْمِ</bdi>, twice
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: How does the iqāmah differ from the adhān?
quduri.back: It's the same, except that after <bdi>حَيَّ عَلَى الفَلَاحِ</bdi> it adds <bdi>قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ</bdi>, twice. The Shāfiʿīs and Ḥanbalīs say its phrases once.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: At what pace are the adhān and the iqāmah said?
quduri.back: The adhān slowly and measured; the iqāmah quickly
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Which way does the muʾadhdhin face, and where does he turn?
quduri.back: Towards the qiblah, though it isn't obligatory. He turns his face to the right for <bdi>حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاةِ</bdi> and to the left for <bdi>حَيَّ عَلَى الفَلَاحِ</bdi>.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Someone has missed several prayers. How does he make the adhān and iqāmah for them?
quduri.back: Both for the first; after that, both, or just the iqāmah
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Why does Qudūrī write <bdi>فَاتَتْهُ صَلَوَاتٌ</bdi>, making the prayers the subject — “prayers escaped him”?
quduri.back: Out of adab
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is the ruling on giving the adhān and iqāmah without wuḍūʾ, or in major impurity?
quduri.back: Best in ritual purity. Without wuḍūʾ it's allowed, though Qudūrī singles out the iqāmah as disliked; giving the adhān in major impurity is disliked.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Which adhān may be given before its time begins?
quduri.back: Fajr's, according to Abū Yūsuf; no other
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.meaning: a precondition: the existence of something depends on it, but it lies outside its essence
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What are the shurūṭ of the prayer, as a group?
quduri.back: All farḍ, and required for the prayer to be valid, but not part of the prayer itself
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.text: The shurūṭ of the prayer: {{c1::purity from ritual and physical impurity}}, {{c2::covering the ʿawrah}}, {{c3::the intention}}, {{c4::the time having entered}}, {{c5::facing the qiblah}} and {{c6::the taḥrīmah}}
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.meaning: the parts of the body that must be covered
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is a man's ʿawrah, for the Ḥanafīs and for the Shāfiʿīs?
quduri.back: For the Ḥanafīs, from below the navel to below the knee, so the knee is included. For the Shāfiʿīs, what's between the navel and the knee, with neither included.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is a free woman's ʿawrah, and what do the Ḥanafīs also exclude?
quduri.back: Everything except the face and hands; the Ḥanafīs also exclude the feet
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is a female slave's ʿawrah?
quduri.back: A man's, plus the belly and back — so her hair, and below her knees, are not ʿawrah
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: How does someone with nothing to cover the ʿawrah pray?
quduri.back: Sitting, gesturing for rukūʿ and sujūd with movements of the head. Standing suffices, but sitting is much better.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: Someone can't find anything to remove an impurity with. What does he do?
quduri.back: He prays with it, and doesn't repeat the prayer
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What must the intention for the prayer be like, and must it be said aloud?
quduri.back: Made for the prayer, with no gap between it and the start of the prayer. Saying it aloud is neither sunnah nor required.
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05

quduri.front: What is the taḥrīmah, and what is discussed about it?
quduri.back: Saying Allāhu akbar to begin the prayer; whether it's a rukn or a sharṭ
quduri.source: Mukhtaṣar al-Qudūrī — Kitāb al-Ṣalāh: times, adhān, shurūṭ — class notes 2026-11-05
